title: 2006 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 3
statement: Prove that, given any formation, each mobot may be colored in one of three colors - say, white, black, and blue - such that no two adjacent clumps of grass are mowed by different mobots of the same color. Two clumps of grass are adjacent if the distance between them is 1 . In your proof, you may use the Four-Color Theorem if you're familiar with it.

solutions.text: We can divide the coordinate plane into regions: Let's say a point belongs to Region 0 if the closest lattice point to it is not on the lawn, and each mobot \(M\) owns a region that is the set of points for which the closest lattice point is on the lawn and mowed by \(M\). Applying the Four-Color Theorem to these regions, we note that all the conditions demanded in the problem are satisfied. In particular at most 3 colors are used on the mobots because every mobot region borders Region 0 and hence is not colored the same color as Region 0.
